statement: What is the solution to the equation $\dfrac{2x + 1}{3} - \dfrac{x - 4}{2} = 2$?

choices.misconception: I multiplied both fractions by $6$ but left the right side as $2$, so I got $x + 14 = 2$ and $x = -12$.
I cleared denominators with $6$ but multiplied the first numerator by $3$ and the second by $2$, getting $3(2x + 1) - 2(x - 4) = 12$, so $4x = 1$.
I multiplied by $6$ correctly but then wrote $-3(x - 4)$ as $-3x - 12$, so I got $x - 10 = 12$ and $x = 22$.

hints: Clear the fractions by multiplying every term by the same number.
Multiply both sides by $6$, the least common denominator. Be careful with the minus sign in front of the second fraction.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
